newsitem.title: UK: LASMO up on Algerian drilling report.
newsitem.headline: LASMO up on Algerian drilling report.

text.p: Shares in LASMO Plc were indicated higher on Tuesday after the UK oil exploration concern announced impressive details on its drilling in Algeria.
By 0718 GMT, the shares were up 5-1/2p to 276.
LASMO posted results from a successful exploration well in the Ghadsames Basin in Algeria, in which it holds a 25 percent working interest in the discovery.
It said the well was drilled to a total depth of 3,310 metres and encountered 14 metres of hydrocarbon bearing sands in the Triassic section.
"Algeria is an important area for LASMO, and this (find) certainly seems to have a very good flow rate," Credit Lyonnais Laing oil analyst Jurjen Lunshof said.
"It could be worth 100 million barrels (per day) to the company," he added.
Yet gains in the stock could be limited with the group set to report its interim results on Thursday.
Estimates vary widely, with pre-exceptional net income forecast between 24 million and 32 million stg, compared with 24 million stg in the year ago period.
Upbeat analysts expect stronger profits to have been fuelled by higher production, but some analysts worried high interest charges could undermine profits.
Additionally, debt levels are poised to rise in 1998 and if gearing levels rise much further, it could preclude a bid for the company, Lunshof added.
